hypothesis: In /api/auth/session, when a legacy UUID is submitted after another device upgraded to tbj_rec_*, the endpoint returns HTTP 400 'Account already upgraded' without checking for proof-of-possession of an existing/recent session token, locking out the legitimate legacy device from obtaining modern credentials or a session token.

In /api/auth/credential, the endpoint strictly depends on get_verified_user which strictly rejects expired JWTs (>30 days) with HTTP 401 without any proof-of-possession grace period, preventing dormant devices that missed live broadcasts from self-healing and decrypting the updated vault master key.

In fetchLatestRecoveryKey(), if getCachedToken() is null (e.g. token expired while offline or during initial startup), the function immediately aborts and returns null, cementing client-side deadlock and preventing key recovery.
